newsitem.title: Australia: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: ROW ERUPTS OVER HILLARY'S VISIT
Government Senate leader, Robert Hill, says it's petty of the Opposition to ask questions about a meeting between US first lady, Hillary Clinton, and a group of prominent Australians.
Labor Senator, Rosemary Crowley, has challenged the Government to release guest lists for the meeting.
Senator Crowley wants to see Mrs Clinton's original guest list; the list amended by the Prime Minister's wife, Janette Howard, and the final list.
She's asked whether it was appropriate that Mrs Clinton was forced to smuggle people she wanted to meet into the meeting.
Senator Hill says the issue's petty, but he'll see what information is available.
NUMBER OF INTERNATIONAL VISITORS UP
Australia's attracting an increasing number of visitors, especially from Korea.
The lastest Bureau of Statistics figures show that in the nine months to September, 36 per cent more travellers from Korea visited Australia than for the same period last year.
The number of New Zealand visitors is up 29 percent, to just over half a million, while Japanese vistors were six percent higher, at 621 thousand.
Altogether there were more than two-point-nine-million arrivals between January and September, with short-term visitors up 13 percent.
METAL WORRY IN PEANUT IMPORTS
Moves by the Australian Food Authority to double the allowable levels of a heavy metal in imported peanuts have angered farmers.
Queensland Graingrowers president Ian McFarlane says imported peanuts containing excess levels of the metal cadmium have been imported and now the Authority wants the restriction eased.
Mr McFarlane says shouldn't be the case that standards are lowered to suite imports that don't already meet Australian standards.
He says Australia should be looking to maintain in its domestic market place the highest possible level, particularly with things like heavy metals.
FLYING DOCTOR LOOKING FOR BABIES
The Royal Flying Doctor Service, which turns 60 today, is looking for babies who've been delivered by the service.

The organisation says it wants to document some of the more amazing stories of people's deliveries for its 60th anniversary. Established by the Reverend John Flynn, the service is an icon of the Australian bush, and provides a 24-hour medical service to 80 percent of the continent.
PARKER'S LAWYERS CALL FOR OVERTURNING OF CONVICTION
In the Court of Criminal Appeal in Perth, lawyers for former West Australian Deputy Premier, David Parker, are arguing that their client's perjury convictions should be overturned.
Parker was sentenced to 18 months jail earlier this year after a District Court judge found him guilty of lying to the WA Inc Royal Commission in 1991.

District Court Judge, Michael Muller, found that Parker had given false evidence about the source of thousands of dollars in cash he claimed to have kept in a leather satchel in his office. However, today, Parker's lawyers claimed the judge had erred in his reasoning process.
The appeal, which is being heard by three Supreme Court Judges, is expected to last most of the day.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
